question: The world's first permanent youth hostel opened in Germany over a hundred years ago and still takes guests today. What kind of building is it in?
source_excerpt: there's still a youth hostel in the castle, although it's now a museum, dedicated to the youth hostel movement

extra.why_interesting: Players picture hostels as cheap, cramped dorms above a bar. In fact the very first one was in a medieval castle, so the budget-travel institution began in a fairy-tale building.
extra.verification_notes: Burg Altena castle (opened 1912) is credited as the first permanent youth hostel and still operates as a DJH hostel, per https://www.thelocal.de/20190516/why-was-germany-home-to-the-worlds-first-youth-hostel/; I couldn't confirm individual-guest booking on the official page.

explanation: It's Altena Castle, where teacher Richard Schirrmann set up dorms so hiking schoolchildren had a cheap place to sleep. The whole hostel movement started with bunk beds behind castle walls.

question: Backpackers call the classic route through Thailand, Laos and Vietnam after a sweet breakfast that guesthouses all along the way cook for Western travellers. What breakfast?
source_excerpt: The name refers to the banana pancakes served at backpacker cafés along the way.

extra.why_interesting: Players expect a famous travel route to be named after a river, a mountain or an explorer. Instead it's named after a breakfast that guesthouses learned would keep backpackers happy, and people can reason their way there.
extra.verification_notes: The Banana Pancake Trail is the well-known backpacker route through Southeast Asia (Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, usually Cambodia), named for the banana pancakes served at backpacker cafés.

explanation: It's known as the Banana Pancake Trail, because cafés along the route learned that homesick backpackers would order banana pancakes every morning.
